18:41 Local Time, 05:41 GMT, 11:11 IST: Alright, folks, it was coming, wasn't it? You could almost smell it from a distance! The game has officially been called off. In fairness, the weather had looked like the pantomime villain of this contest ever since two days ago, and it eventually lived up to that billing. The rain did relent for a few brief spells, giving us a glimmer of hope, but it was merely playing hide-and-seek with us. And so, the series scoreline remains 2-0 in India's favour, meaning the visitors can no longer lose the series. New Zealand can still fight back to level things up, but they will have to do so without a few of their key players, who will now head out to join the Test squad.

The umpires have had a long, hard look at the conditions and decided that play won't be possible today. They walked across to both captains and conveyed the decision. The players are now shaking hands and exchanging smiles as the inevitable is confirmed. The groundstaff having their share of fun as they dance around with the mop sticks.

Righto! This will be the last outing for several players from both sides who have been named in their respective Test squads, as they switch gears and begin preparations for the longer format. Looking at the names in those squads, New Zealand (Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Henry Nicholls, Tom Latham and Nathan Smith) arguably stand to be more affected by these departures than India (Shubman Gill and KL Rahul). On a brighter note, the weather forecast at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui looks much more promising, with the final two games scheduled for Friday and Sunday. Hopefully, we get plenty of uninterrupted cricket there. Do join us for both encounters. Until then, cheers and goodbye from the trio of Raju Peethala, Ramakrishnan MS and Venkatesh AV. Ciao!!
